feedback.answered: Initial A1/A2 connection: leader append replies update tracked match and may advance the commit index, while maybeCommit checks the current term through raftLog and the tracker. send routes append and vote responses through msgsAfterAppend; RawNode transfers those responses to storage completion messages or the synchronous Ready/Advance path. Thus persistence completion qualifies support before its consumer counts it. Authority transitions reset votes, replication progress and readOnly state; term dispatch rejects old responses, with an explicit exception allowing completed snapshots from old storage messages while refusing to stabilize their appended entries. These are implementation observations, not a complete correctness argument. Two sourced unresolved surfaces are retained: (1) stepLeader releases pendingReadIndexMessages when MsgAppResp advances commit, whereas switchToConfig can advance commit and broadcasts without that release. The queue is populated when a multi-voter leader has no current-term committed entry. A legal history reaching configuration-driven first current-term commit, and whether a later independent path guarantees release, remain unknown. (2) README caller instructions permit sending messages while same-batch entries persist, but Ready.Entries and Ready.Messages require storing entries before messages. The synchronous RawNode path places external msgsAfterAppend into Ready.Messages. This is a document/interface conflict to investigate, not permission to choose the weaker policy for a finding.
